message.content:
LeBron James is an American professional basketball player widely regarded as one of the greatest athletes in the history of the sport. He was born on December 30, 1984, in Akron, Ohio, and rose to prominence as a high school phenom at St. Vincent‑St. Mary High School. LeBron was selected first overall in the 2003 NBA Draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers, where he quickly became a dominant force.

He has played for the Cleveland Cavaliers (2003–2010, 2014–2018), Miami Heat (2010–2014), and Los Angeles Lakers (2018–present). LeBron has won four NBA championships—two with Miami (2012, 2013), one with Cleveland (2016), and one with Los Angeles (2020)—and earned four NBA Most Valuable Player awards (2009, 2010, 2012, 2013). He has been named to the All‑NBA First Team 17 times and has been selected for the NBA All‑Star Game 19 times, setting a record for most selections.

Beyond his on‑court achievements, LeBron is known for his philanthropy, notably the LeBron James Family Foundation, which opened the “I Promise” school in Akron. He has also pursued a career in entertainment, producing films and television shows through his company SpringHill Entertainment.
